parts.watchFor: Lut is sent to cities that rob travellers and do shameful things openly. Watch how they answer him.

questions.q: What did the people of the cities do?
options: They robbed travellers and did shameful things openly

questions.q: How did they answer Lut's warnings?
options: They mocked him: bring God's punishment, if you are truthful

lesson.text: Lut kept warning his people for years, even though almost no one listened. When wrongdoing becomes open and proud, a believer still speaks up, calmly and clearly, and keeps himself apart from it.
lesson.curious: Muslims honour Lut, known in the Bible as Lot, for warning his people patiently even when almost no one listened.

reflect.muslim: Is there something wrong that has become normal around you? How can you keep apart from it without looking down on anyone?
reflect.curious: What does it take to keep speaking up when almost no one listens?

parts.act: Stay apart from one thing your friends do that you know is wrong, without lecturing them.

parts.watchFor: Lut receives guests his people mean to harm. Watch how he protects them.

options: Angels in the form of young men

questions.q: What did Lut say to the crowd at his door?
options: Fear God, and do not disgrace me before my guests

questions.q: What were Lut and his family told as they left by night?
options: Run as fast as you can
Let none of you look back

lesson.text: Lut stood at his door to protect his guests, alone, and help came from God. His own wife stayed behind, because her heart was with her people: being close to a prophet saves no one whose heart is elsewhere.
lesson.curious: In this story Lut protects his guests at great risk. Muslims also learn from his wife that family ties alone do not save anyone; what is in the heart does.

reflect.muslim: Where is your heart, really? Is anything pulling it back toward what you've left behind?
reflect.curious: What would you risk to protect someone who trusted you?

parts.act: Look out for someone who's new or alone this week, and make them feel safe.

parts.watchFor: Morning comes to the cities of the plain. Watch what remains.

questions.q: What happened to the cities at sunrise?
options: A mighty blast seized them and they were overturned

questions.q: What lies where the cities stood, according to tradition?
options: A sea so salty nothing lives in it
Lut and those who believed with him

lesson.text: The cities were overturned, and their place became a sign for people who think. Lut and those who believed were saved. God's patience is long, but ruins remind us it is not endless.
lesson.curious: Muslims read the stories of destroyed cities as reminders: people are given time to change, and those who listen are saved.

carry.title: A prayer for good in this life and the next

reflect.muslim: Which reminders around you have you stopped noticing?
reflect.curious: Why do you think the Quran points to ruins as reminders?

parts.act: Remember someone who has passed away and pray for them this week.
